chapter: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band
title: Louisville band alumni in Lloyd Scott's and Furman Tapp's bands
summary: Les Carr, Dickie Wells, Hal MacFerin, Bill Beason and Mac Walker came out of the Louisville kid band and played in Furman Tapp's and Lloyd Scott's bands, so half of Scott's band was from Louisville.

bands.name: Booker T. Washington Community Center Band

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh, we had a guy named Les Carr, played clarinet and sax. He was out of the band. Of course in the band we had no sax, he played clarinet.
But later he played clarinet and sax. Well, he used to play with a band around there called Furman
Yeah. Played in Small's Paradise over there.
But before that, he was from Louisville, you know.

He was from Louisville and he had a band, he got some of the kids out of the band, Sunday school band, and had an orchestra. So -- but how they got away with -- which was Cecil Scott's band in later years, that was Lloyd Scott's band, his brother, Lloyd Scott.
Yeah, Lloyd had it. Lloyd was a drummer.

A drummer. And they took Dickie, come in and they needed a trombone. They needed Dickie Wells. The next day they needed a saxophone so they got Les Carr, alto and clarinet, and they needed a tenor, and they got Hal MacFarland. He's a tenor and clarinet.
MacFerin, F-e-r-i-n. And then they got

him, and then when -- I think when Cecil left -- when Lloyd left, I think Beason went in there. They had practically -- then they had another bass player in there, Mac Walker. He was out of the band, too, out of the kid band.
He later played with Stuff at the Onyx Club.
So they had half that band almost was out of Kentucky, out of Louisville.
